title: The observation request
description: Asks the running sketch to be observed. The writer places this atomically by way of a temporary file, and id changes with every request (ADR-0018 decision 3). With count at 2 or more, shots are taken in succession without stopping the frame loop, and the catalogue is written last. **A request whose id can be read is always answered**: one that cannot be read otherwise (a scale, count or every of the wrong type, such as "0.5" or true, or a count or every that is not a whole number, such as 2.5) takes no shot, the previous products are cleared, and the reply carries the reason in warnings. A request whose id cannot be read (missing, not a string, or text that is not JSON) gets no reply, and a request whose id was already answered is not processed again (see id). **A key this version does not read does not fail the request**: the sketch takes the shot without it and the reply's warnings name the key (a misspelt scale, as in sacle, is not read as scale), also when the request cannot be read for another reason. The keys listed here are the whole set, so a writer that adds a key updates this schema first (additionalProperties is false).

id.description: This request's identifier. The reply echoes it back. A request with an id already seen is not processed again, even after the sketch relaunches: the answer left in the reply is the record. Do not reuse an id while the facet remains. **This includes a request that could not be read**: once it is answered, fixing it and placing it again under the same id is not processed — place the fixed request with a new id. **A reply that echoes another id is not yours.** The facet keeps one request and one report, so when another writer places a request over yours, your id may never come back: if `request.json` no longer holds your request and the reply echoes an id that is neither yours nor the one it echoed just before you placed it, your request was either answered and then overwritten, or replaced before it was read. Which of the two cannot be told from the reply.

scale.description: How far to scale the written image down (1 = full size). 1 when omitted, and null reads as omitted. A scale outside this range is never replaced in silence: above 1, or at or below 0, the image is written at full size and the reply's warnings say so. This holds however large the number is (1e400 too).

count.description: How many shots to take. 1 when omitted, and null reads as omitted. Asking outside the range is never clamped in silence: the count used, and whether the ceiling or the floor cut it, appear in the reply's warnings. This holds however large the number is (1e19, or -1e400 for the floor): it is not an unreadable request.

every.description: Take a shot every this many frames. Every frame when omitted, and null reads as omitted. Asking outside the range is never clamped in silence, as with count, however large the number is. **Counted in frames rather than seconds**, so the shots follow the frames the sketch actually draws. The sketch being observed runs on the wall clock unless it chose `clock: .frames`, and writing the images makes frames heavier, so **the shots are not evenly spaced in time** — lay the series out by each entry's `time` in the catalogue (frames), rather than assuming an even gap. For motion with evenly spaced times, write it with `mokume render` instead: it runs the sketch at a fixed frame rate and writes every frame, so nothing needs laying out again.

keep.description: Keep the one image taken, together with the conditions known for its frame, outside this facet, in `.mokume/kept/<id>/` (`kept-frame.schema.json`), where the next request does not clear it. false when omitted, and null reads as omitted; **a request without it is answered exactly as before**, byte for byte. A value that is not a boolean ("yes", 1) makes the request unreadable. Only a single shot is kept: with a count above 1 the shots are taken but not kept, and the reply's warnings say so. The id becomes the folder's name, so an id holding a slash or NUL, starting with a dot, ending in `.partial` (in any letter case), or too long for a folder name is not kept (warnings say why). A folder of that name that already exists — even an empty one, or one whose name differs only in letter case on a volume that ignores case — is never overwritten or removed, and when `.mokume/kept` itself is a symbolic link or a file it is not followed or removed and nothing is kept. The folder is written as `<id>.<pid>.partial` and renamed to `<id>` only once the image and the catalogue are in place and synced, so a `.partial` folder is unfinished. When the picture was changed after its frame was drawn (a callback drew while the sketch was stopped), it is not the picture of that frame, so it is not kept. The reply's `kept` names the folder when it was kept; without it, warnings say why. Older sketches ignore this key and name it in warnings.

time.description: Draw exactly one frame at these seconds before taking it. Rounded to Float. deltaTime is zero and frameCount advances once. The picture is shown and draw side effects remain; this is not a rewind. Only draw() reads this time: input callbacks read the author's clock, and a playing video or a recorded sound does not keep this time as its position or start. Only count=1 and every=1 are allowed. noLoop stays stopped; external pause and recording refuse the request. Omit it to observe normally; null reads the same as omitted, but a sketch older than this schema refuses a null time (it reads it as a time of the wrong type), so omitting is the safe way. Check appliedTime and frames[0].time in the reply; older sketches may ignore this key.
